page: The UpCloud STARTER-1xCPU-4GB is an entry-level virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with a single shared vCPU utilizing the x86_64 architecture, powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The hardware allocation includes 4.0 GB of system memory, 30 GB of local SSD storage, and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The underlying CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, AES cryptography, and SHA extensions, which assist in accelerating specific cryptographic and mathematical operations.

Performance benchmarks reveal a significant divergence between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. In single-core stress-ng tests, the server achieves top-tier performance, and its single-threaded compression and decompression speeds for gzip and bzip3 also rank in the top 10% of tested hardware. Conversely, because the instance relies on a single shared vCPU, its multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is also a limiting factor, with PassMark memory scores in the bottom 10% and read bandwidths categorized as weak.

This server offers a highly cost-efficient profile for workloads that do not require sustained multi-core processing or high memory throughput. The resource density is optimized for lightweight utility tasks rather than heavy data processing. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, software development environments, lightweight single-threaded applications, and simple background cron jobs. It is not recommended for database hosting, large-scale LLM inference, or memory-intensive applications.
description: The UpCloud STARTER-1xCPU-4GB is a budget-friendly, shared-resource virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by a single shared AMD EPYC 9575F vCPU clocked at 2.0 GHz, it features 4.0 GB of RAM and 30 GB of local SSD storage. While its single-core performance is highly competitive—ranking in the top tier for stress-ng single-core and single-threaded compression benchmarks—its multi-core capabilities and memory bandwidth are heavily constrained, placing them in the lower performance tiers. This resource profile makes the server highly cost-efficient for lightweight, single-threaded applications, development environments, and basic web serving, while rendering it unsuitable for resource-intensive databases or multi-threaded workloads.
